data.name: Qaim
data.gender_notes: Qaim is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is established or upright in his faith and deeds, fulfilling his responsibilities and duties. The name Qaim carries the meaning “Established, Upright” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Qaim usually hope their child will grow to embody established, upright and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In the Quran, Qaim refers to the Last Prophet, Muhammad (peace be upon him), who will be the first to rise from the dead on the Day of Judgment.
data.etymology: Qaim belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Established, Upright.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Qaim total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: قائم
in_arabic.long_meaning: قائم هو اسم عربي مشتق من الفعل قام الذي يعني القيام أو الوقوف، ويشير إلى الشخص الذي يقوم بشيء أو يحققه، وله أهمية دينية وثقافية في الإسلام حيث يوصف به الإمام المهدي في الاعتقاد الشيعي

in_urdu.name: قائم

in_english.name: Qaim
in_english.meaning: the one who rises or stands
in_english.long_meaning: Qaim means the one who rises or stands, derived from the Arabic root q-w-m, it refers to a person who establishes or upholds something, and has religious significance in Islam, particularly in Shia belief as a title for Imam Mahdi

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Qaim' holds a significant cultural value in the Islamic society as it symbolizes righteousness, strength, and leadership. The belief in an Imam Mahdi, the awaited leader and savior of the Muslim Ummah, who will re-establish justice and peace on earth, stems from this name. The title of Qaim is attributed to this promised leader, reinforcing the idea of striving for virtuous leadership and upholding faith and moral values in the community.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Qaim signifies a deep connection to one's faith and commitment to leading an upright and moral life. It not only implies the fulfillment of religious obligations but also emphasizes the importance of personal responsibility, resilience, and character in conforming to the divine will. The Arabic root-words emphasize the constant striving for progress and growth, both inwardly as well as outwardly, as key elements of Islamic spirituality.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Established, Upright" symbolizes One who is established or upright in his faith and deeds, fulfilling his responsibilities and duties.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Qaim serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of established, upright.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Qaim is mentioned in the book "The History of the Prophets and Kings" by Ibn al-Athir. The name Qaim carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The name Qaim is mentioned as one of the names of the Prophet Muhammad's companions.

trends: increasing popularity in the Middle East
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Qaim remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.

name_in_real_life.story: A successful entrepreneur named Hassan Qaim in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia attributes much of their success to the blessing of their name Qaim, which means "Established, Upright". They believe their name has shaped their identity and guided them through life.
